resources.string: Churn rewrites your router\'s IMEIs. Rewriting an IMEI is a criminal offense in some countries, for example under the UK\'s Mobile Telephones (Re-programming) Act 2002. Check the law where you use the router.
Churn only protects you if you follow its rules every time. You can read them again from the router screen.

string-array.name: rules_always
string-array.item: At home, at work and anywhere else you return to, keep the router switched off or without a SIM.
Before you get to such a place, unplug everything and switch the router off.
Connect to the router by cable only, and keep its Wi-Fi off.
Use normal SIM cards, or eSIM adapter cards with one profile each, and put them only into SIM slot 2. Don\'t use the router\'s built-in eSIM.
Send all traffic through the router\'s VPN, and don\'t use the router without it.
Do not run the router without the battery installed.
Before you leave a place you return to with the router, remove the SIM card or disable the eSIM profile in every phone, tablet, watch or laptop you carry, and keep it that way until you\'re back.

Use the router only with devices that run Linux, or an Android system built for privacy, such as GrapheneOS. That rules out Windows, macOS, iPhones, iPads, Chromebooks and the Android that most phones and tablets come with.

resources.string: For maximum privacy, also follow these rules where you can:

string-array.name: rules_where_you_can
string-array.item: Use SIM cards that aren\'t registered to your name. The same goes for eSIM profiles.
Get each new SIM card or eSIM profile from a different provider than the last one. If you can\'t, start using the new one somewhere else and some days after you stopped using the last one.
Don\'t reuse a card once you\'ve swapped it out. If you run out of new cards, keep using the current one until you get a new one.
Vary when you swap SIMs, and where you switch the radio on and off.
Pay for the VPN in a way that isn\'t tied to your name.
Block SIM slot 1, for example with a drop of hot glue.

Trust it only if this is your router and no other device is connected to the cable.

The router identifies itself with a key Churn hasn't seen before:

%1$s

This happens after a factory reset or firmware upgrade without kept settings. It can also mean that another device answers in the router's place. Trust the new key only if you know why it changed.

Churn keeps a folder on the router, /etc/churn/, with a random secret, the router's IMEIs as its factory IMEIs, and a script that writes them back. A firmware upgrade that keeps settings keeps the folder; a factory reset deletes it.

The router's IMEIs are:
IMEI 1: %1$s
IMEI 2: %2$s
These IMEIs don\'t have the Mudi 7\'s type allocation code, so they may already have been rewritten, for example by blue-merle. Churn would restore exactly these.
An IMEI has a wrong check digit, so it may already have been rewritten.
These are IMEIs Churn wrote, but Churn\'s folder on the router is gone, for example after a firmware upgrade. Setting up again would record them as the factory IMEIs.
Churn\'s secret on the router is gone. Setting up creates a new one, so each card gets new IMEIs.
Slot 2 is on the SIM 2 tray.
Slot 2 is on the built-in eSIM.
The IMEIs aren\'t the ones Churn wrote last. A firmware upgrade or reset may have restored the factory IMEIs; the next swap writes new ones.
GL\'s scheduled reboot is on. Turn it off in GL\'s web interface: a reboot is a power-on, so with a SIM inside it registers wherever it happens.
The Enhanced Kill Switch is off, so traffic can bypass the VPN. Turn it on in GL\'s VPN settings (rule 5).
The factory IMEIs are back, and airplane mode is on.

Churn turns airplane mode on and writes the factory IMEIs back:

IMEI 1: %1$s
IMEI 2: %2$s
Churn forgets the router\'s key and password. Its folder on the router stays.

Churn turns airplane mode on, gives the router random throwaway IMEIs, sets slot 2 to the built-in eSIM with no profile enabled, and shuts the router down. Keep the cable connected until the router is off.\n\nWhy: a card in slot 2 registers at every power-on, whatever airplane mode says, so the new card must stay off until it has its own IMEIs. While slot 2 is on the built-in eSIM, the card in the SIM 2 tray stays off. The eSIM\'s short bursts at the next power-on then carry the throwaway IMEIs, not the old card\'s.
\"Power On with Charger\" is off in GL\'s settings. Otherwise plugging in a charger switches the router on, wherever you are.

1. Wait until the router is off, then unplug the cable.
2. Take out the battery and replace the card in the SIM 2 tray with the new one. Leave the SIM 1 tray empty.
3. Put the battery back.
4. Go to a place you don't return to, away from where you used the old card.
5. Switch the router on, connect the cable and tap Continue.

Why: at power-on only the built-in eSIM's short bursts go out, with the throwaway IMEIs and a test identity that is likely the same on every Mudi 7.

If you keep the old card after all, Continue gives it back its own IMEIs.
Give the new card its IMEIs
Churn waits until the router\'s radio is off, sets slot 2 to the SIM 2 tray, reads the new card\'s ICCID and writes the IMEIs that belong to it. The radio stays off throughout.

The router has the new card's IMEIs, and its radio stays off until you turn airplane mode off, on the router's screen or in GL's web interface.

Turn it off later, at another place and time, and never at home, at work or another place you return to.

Why: the old card went quiet where you started the swap. If the new one starts where and when the old one stopped, the two are easy to match.
Throwaway IMEIs written and read back.
Slot 2 is on the built-in eSIM.
Waiting until the router has started and its radio is off. This takes about two minutes after power-on.
Slot 2 is on the SIM 2 tray.
The card\'s IMEIs are written and read back.
The router gave an answer Churn didn\'t expect, so Churn stopped. Nothing after the last line above is assumed done.
The router\'s radio isn\'t off, so Churn stopped.
GL\'s scheduled reboot is on. Turn it off in GL\'s web interface first: a reboot is a power-on, so with a SIM inside it registers wherever it happens.
The router didn\'t keep the IMEIs Churn wrote.
The built-in eSIM\'s profile is still enabled.

Churn found no usable card in the SIM 2 tray: no card at all, or an eSIM adapter card without an enabled profile. Slot 2 is back on the built-in eSIM, so you can switch the router off, check the card, switch the router on again and tap Try again.
